evidence: Full CDIAL kāla explicitly gives Sindhi kāro, West Pahari kāo/kāwo, Maithili kariyā, Hindi kālā/kāliyā, Marwari kāḷo, Gujarati kāḷũ/kāḷiyũ and Marathi kāḷā black. The selected survey kāl-/kar-/kaw- variants and ordinary -iya/final-vowel forms fit this regional family, preserving vowels, gemination, lateral/rhotic/stop notation and local secondary lateral syllables. Those secondary forms are family assignments, not new ancient suffix reconstructions. Cross-IA transmission and local phonetic/ending histories remain qualified; full same-family slash responses retain all variants. Turner’s possible Dravidian origin is not replaced by a new donor claim.
